questions.text: On which date did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) deliver his Last Sermon?
questions.explanation: He delivered the Last Sermon on the ninth of Dhul Hijjah, 10 years after Hijrat.

questions.text: Where was the Last Sermon delivered?
questions.explanation: It was delivered in the Uranah valley of Mount Arafat.

questions.text: In which year after Hijrat was the Last Sermon delivered?
questions.explanation: It was delivered 10 years after Hijrat.

questions.text: In the Last Sermon, what did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declare sacred?
options: Life, property and honour of every Muslim
questions.explanation: He said your blood, property and honour are as sacred as this day, this month and this city.

questions.text: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about usury (riba)?
questions.explanation: 'Usury is forbidden' — he began by remitting the interest due to Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib.

questions.text: Whose interest claims did the Prophet (PBUH) remit first?
questions.explanation: He remitted entirely the interest Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib had to receive.

questions.text: Regarding women, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said:
questions.explanation: 'O people! Fear Allah concerning women' — he stressed their rights.

questions.text: The Last Sermon told Muslims to worship Allah, offer five prayers, fast in Ramadan and:
questions.explanation: He recommended five prayers, fasting in Ramadan and paying Zakat.

questions.text: Major Tufail Muhammad was given the task of retrieving which village?
questions.explanation: He was assigned to retrieve the village Lakshmipur in East Pakistan from Indian occupation.

questions.text: When did Major Tufail Muhammad embrace martyrdom?
questions.explanation: He embraced martyrdom on 7th August 1958.

questions.text: Into how many groups did Major Tufail divide his men?
questions.explanation: He divided his men into three groups.

questions.text: Rashid Minhas was the only officer of which force to receive the Nishan-e-Haider?
questions.explanation: Rashid Minhas was the only PAF officer to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

questions.text: When was Rashid Minhas born?
questions.explanation: He was born on 17th February 1951.

questions.text: Rashid Minhas is the youngest person to receive the:
questions.explanation: He was the youngest and shortest-serving officer to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

questions.text: On which date did Rashid Minhas's training flight incident happen?
questions.explanation: On August 20, 1971, his instructor tried to seize control of the aircraft.

questions.text: Where did Rashid Minhas join as a flying cadet?
questions.explanation: At 17 he joined the Pakistan Air Force Academy in Risalpur as a flying cadet.

questions.text: According to the poem 'A Nation's Strength', what does NOT make a nation strong?
questions.explanation: 'It is not gold' — kingdoms built on gold go down in battle shock.

questions.text: In the poem, kingdoms built on gold have their shafts laid on:
questions.explanation: 'Its shafts are laid on sinking sand, not on abiding rock.'

questions.text: What does the poet say about the sword?
options: Empires built on it passed away into red dust
questions.explanation: 'Ask the red dust of empires passed away' — the sword did not keep empires alive.

questions.text: Who builds a nation's pillars deep, according to the poem?
options: Men who work while others sleep
questions.explanation: 'Brave men who work while others sleep, who dare while others fly, they build a nation's pillars deep.'

questions.text: The central idea of 'A Nation's Strength' is that a nation's true strength lies in:
questions.explanation: Not gold, sword or pride, but men of truth and honour make a nation strong.

questions.text: The word 'throng' means:
questions.explanation: The glossary defines throng as a large, densely packed crowd of people.

questions.text: When and where was Quaid-e-Azam born?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on December 25, 1876 in Karachi.

questions.text: Why was Muhammad Ali Jinnah called Quaid-e-Azam?
options: For his far-sightedness and leadership qualities
questions.explanation: He was known as Quaid-e-Azam because of his far-sightedness and leadership qualities.

questions.text: In his early politics, Jinnah was a proponent of:
questions.explanation: In the early days of his politics he was a proponent of Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.text: In which year did the Congress agree to a separate electorate after the Lucknow Pact?
questions.explanation: The Congress agreed to a separate electorate for the first time in 1916, after the Lucknow Pact.

questions.text: Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points were presented in reaction to:
questions.explanation: The famous Fourteen Points were introduced in reaction to the Nehru Report.

questions.text: Where were the Round Table Conferences held (1930-32)?
questions.explanation: The Round Table Conferences were held in London from 1930 to 1932.

questions.text: The idea that Hindus and Muslims are two separate nations is called the:
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam was well aware of the Two-Nation Theory: Hindus and Muslims are two nations.

questions.text: Smog is a mixture of:
questions.explanation: The word smog was coined from a mixture of smoke and fog.

questions.text: In which months does smog slow down everything in Punjab?
questions.explanation: During December and January smog slows down everything.

questions.text: Which province of Pakistan is most affected by smog?
questions.explanation: Punjab is the most affected out of all provinces.

questions.text: Which city, once called the city of gardens, has been named one of the most polluted cities?
questions.explanation: Lahore, the provincial capital, has been called one of the most polluted cities in the world.

questions.text: Why has the problem of smog intensified in recent decades?
questions.explanation: Rapid industrialisation and thousands of vehicles have intensified the problem.

questions.text: Which disease can smog cause?
questions.explanation: Smog particles cause diseases including asthma, strokes, heart attacks and lung cancer.

questions.text: According to the lesson, poor air quality results in:
questions.explanation: The better the air quality, the better our mental health; poor air quality harms it.

questions.text: Samina Baig is the first Pakistani woman to reach the top of which peak (2nd highest in the world)?
questions.explanation: She reached the top of the 8611-metre K2, the 2nd highest peak in the world.

questions.text: In which year did Samina Baig climb Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: In 2013 Samina became the first Pakistani woman to climb Mount Everest.

questions.text: Who trained Samina Baig in mountaineering?
questions.explanation: She was trained in mountaineering by her brother Mirza Ali.

questions.text: How many summits on seven continents did Samina Baig scale?
questions.explanation: She is the only Pakistani woman to scale the seven summits on seven continents, in eight months.

questions.text: Aconcagua, climbed by Samina Baig, is the highest peak in:
questions.explanation: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest peak in South America.

questions.text: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest peak in:
questions.explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest peak in Africa.

questions.text: Why did Mirza Ali let his sister reach the Everest summit alone?
options: To present a message of empowerment to the women of Pakistan
questions.explanation: He stopped short to present a message of empowerment to all women of Pakistan.

questions.text: The word 'Adha' is an Arabic word meaning:
questions.explanation: Adha is an Arabic word for sacrifice.

questions.text: What did Allah send instead of Hazrat Ismail (AS) to be sacrificed?
questions.explanation: Allah sent the angel Jibrail with a ram to sacrifice instead of his son.

questions.text: Who tried to stop Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) from obeying Allah's command?
questions.explanation: Satan attempted to confuse and tempt Hazrat Ibrahim, but he drove him away.

questions.text: About how long after Eid-ul-Fitr does Eid-ul-Adha come?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Adha takes place about two months after Eid-ul-Fitr.

questions.text: How is the meat of the sacrificial animal divided?
options: Equally among family, friends and the needy
questions.explanation: The meat is divided equally among family, friends and the needy.

questions.text: Which two children ask their parents questions about Eid-ul-Adha?
questions.explanation: Zainab and Saliha ask their parents different questions about the festival.

questions.text: In which country is 'The Wise Old Woman' set?
questions.explanation: The story is set in a small village in the western hills of Japan.

questions.text: What was the cruel lord's decree?
options: Anyone over seventy-one must be left in the mountains
questions.explanation: Anyone over seventy-one was to be banished and left in the mountains to die.

questions.text: Why did the old mother break off twigs on the way up the mountain?
options: To mark the way so her son would not get lost
questions.explanation: She said she was marking the way so her son would not get lost returning.

questions.text: Where did the farmer hide his mother?
options: In a secret room dug under the kitchen floor
questions.explanation: He dug a deep hole in the kitchen floor and made a small room to hide her.

questions.text: Which lord threatened to conquer the village?
questions.explanation: Lord Higa of the town beyond the hills threatened to take the village.

questions.text: How did the old woman make a drum that sounds without being beaten?
options: Put a bumblebee inside a paper drum
questions.explanation: Make a drum with paper sides and put a bumblebee inside; as it tries to escape it beats the sides.

questions.text: What did the young lord realise at the end?
options: He had been very wrong; the old are wise
questions.explanation: He said, 'I have been very wrong' and learned that the old woman was wiser than all his wise men.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Think Not All is Over'?
questions.explanation: The poem is by Harriet Stowe.

questions.text: What returns after autumn, according to the poem?
questions.explanation: 'Think not all is over, spring returneth; buds and leaves and blossoms thou shalt see.'

questions.text: What sleeps in the frozen buds of every winter?
options: The blossoms of a future flower
questions.explanation: 'In the frozen buds of every winter sleep the blossoms of a future flower.'

questions.text: 'For a night alone endureth, God at last shall bring a ___ hour.'
questions.explanation: Night does not last; God at last shall bring a morning hour.

questions.text: The main message of 'Think Not All is Over' is:
options: Never lose hope; bad times pass
questions.explanation: The poem teaches hope: after hardship, good times return.

questions.text: The word 'wailing' means:
options: crying with pain, grief or anger
questions.explanation: The glossary gives wailing as crying with pain, grief or anger.

questions.text: What was the name of the boy's father's business?
questions.explanation: His father owned the Glenn Plumbing Company.

questions.text: What was the boy called by his family?
questions.explanation: His father asked, 'You want to go up, Bud?'

questions.text: How old was the boy when he first flew in a plane?
questions.explanation: It was the summer he turned eight.

questions.text: What kind of plane did they fly in?
questions.explanation: A man had an old open-cockpit biplane and was taking people up.

questions.text: Which famous pilot had crossed the Atlantic Ocean two years earlier?
questions.explanation: Everybody knew about Charles Lindbergh's Atlantic crossing flight two years earlier.

questions.text: How did the boy feel after the flight?
questions.explanation: When he got out of the plane he was elated.

questions.text: From the air, the buildings looked like:
options: a toy train set in a store
questions.explanation: Everything on the ground looked small, like a train set in a store.

questions.text: According to Allama Iqbal, culture encompasses all the:
options: mental, spiritual and physical activities of a nation
questions.explanation: Iqbal said culture encompasses all the mental, spiritual and physical activities of a nation.

questions.text: Pakistani culture is mainly inspired by:
questions.explanation: Pakistan is an ideological Islamic state, and its culture is inspired by Islam.

questions.text: About what percentage of Pakistanis speak Punjabi as a first language, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: Punjabi is spoken as a first language by 44% of Pakistanis.

questions.text: Phulkari is associated with the costumes of:
questions.explanation: Punjab is known for the use of phulkari in its costumes.

questions.text: Which is a traditional Punjabi dish mentioned in the lesson?
options: Sarson ka saag and makai ki roti
questions.explanation: Dishes exclusive to Punjab include parathas, makai ki roti and sarson ka saag.

questions.text: Which sports are Punjabis especially fond of, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: Punjabi people are fond of kabaddi and wrestling.

questions.text: Media is known as the ___ pillar of democracy.
questions.explanation: Media is known as the fourth pillar of democracy.

questions.text: Media is considered the ___ of modern society.
questions.explanation: Media is considered the mirror of modern society.

questions.text: Where do newspapers usually publish public opinion?
questions.explanation: Public opinion is reflected in letters to the editor, published on a separate page.

questions.text: Electronic media was born with the invention of the:
questions.explanation: The birth of electronic media took place with the invention of the radio.

questions.text: Which of these is a social media network named in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Facebook, YouTube, Twitter and Instagram are named as social media networks.

questions.text: Print media provides great incentive to business through:
questions.explanation: Print media helps business through a large number of advertisements.
